source_evidence: These fees and expenses may be significant and will reduce the value of your account and the return on your investment.
answer: Variable annuity costs can come from several sources. The insurer may charge a base contract fee and administrative fees; the mutual funds you choose also have underlying fund fees. Optional insurance benefits can add fees, and a surrender charge may apply if you withdraw money during a specified period. Other charges, such as sales loads or transfer fees, may also apply. Because these costs can reduce both your account value and investment returns, review the contract’s prospectus and ask which fees apply.
